statements.status_notes: On Linux 6.15 and later, libmount's detached-tree path for X-mount.subdir passed the configured subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW only, which does not stop symlinks in intermediate path components, so a local user allowed an fstab X-mount.subdir mount could attach a host path at the mountpoint. The code was added in util-linux 2.42. Upstream fixed it in util-linux 2.42.3 (commit https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/commit/ce4e181aa967a06079851410d82ca4428341ba7b); see https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/security/advisories/GHSA-8f2p-47x3-43mv and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-78409. Checked the libmount library in every published build of the DHI Alpine 3.24 util-linux packages (2.42-r0, 2.42.1-r0, 2.42.3-r0 (published for aarch64 only) and 2.42.3-r1) on x86_64 and aarch64. These packages are built from the upstream release tarball for their version, with Alpine's packaging patches, and each libmount reports that upstream version. 2.42-r0 and 2.42.1-r0 (util-linux 2.42.0 and 2.42.1) are affected. 2.42.3-r0 and 2.42.3-r1 (util-linux 2.42.3) include the fix; their libmount also carries the debug message the fix adds ('X-mount.subdir is root, ignoring'), which the earlier builds lack. The range ends at 2.42.3-r0.
